overall.assessment: Prema prikazanom sadržaju, podcast je uglavnom usmjeren evanđeoski: povezuje molitvu i Kristovu muku s Božjim milosrđem, obraćenjem i odgovornim vršenjem Božje volje. Dobro je što Isusa ne prikazuje samo kao milosrdnog Spasitelja nego i kao suca, no formulacija „bez suda nema milosrđa” traži pažljivo tumačenje kako se Božja pravednost ne bi prikazala kao suprotnost milosrđu ili kao puko kažnjavanje. Naglasak na farizejskom duhu, grijehu protiv Duha Svetoga i ustrajnosti može potaknuti ozbiljan ispit savjesti, ali pastoralno zahtijeva razlikovanje tvrdokornog odbijanja obraćenja od sumnje, slabosti ili iskrene poteškoće u vjeri. Budući da su javna molitva, knjiga i domoljubna inicijativa predstavljene samo kao najave, njihovu konkretnu provedbu i odnos prema općem dobru nije moguće procijeniti iz sažetka.
seeds_of_logos: Krunica Božjega milosrđa, litanije i razmatranje žalosnih otajstava stavljaju Kristovu muku i povjerenje u Božje milosrđe u središte zajedničke pobožnosti; kršćanska molitva uključuje slavljenje, prošnju i zagovor te treba oblikovati život, a ne ostati samo vanjski čin.

Poticanje na svakodnevno pitanje „Što ja trebam danas činiti?” povezuje vjeru s konkretnim moralnim djelovanjem i vršenjem Božje volje. To je važan antropološki naglasak: čovjek nije samo primatelj utjehe nego slobodna i odgovorna osoba pozvana odgovoriti na Božju ljubav.
Prikaz Isusova ulaska u sukob s farizejima kao poziva na njihovo obraćenje može čuvati evanđeosku nadu da upozorenje nije samo osuda: Kristova milost poziva grešnika da se vrati Bogu.

Poziv na javnu krunicu može biti legitiman oblik zajedničkog svjedočenja vjere i sudjelovanja vjernika u javnom životu, pod uvjetom da poštuje ljudsko dostojanstvo i ne instrumentalizira vjeru u političke svrhe.
concerns: Tvrdnja „bez suda nema milosrđa” može biti teološki plodna ako znači da milosrđe ozbiljno shvaća istinu o grijehu, odgovornosti i obraćenju. Postaje rizična ako sugerira da je sud prvenstveno prijetnja ili da se Božja pravda i milosrđe međusobno isključuju: katoličko razumijevanje povezuje ih u Božjem spasenjskom djelovanju, a pokajani grešnik može se pouzdati u milosrdnu pravdu Božju.

Izraz „kad je Božje djelo očito, nema više izgovora” i govor o grijehu protiv Duha Svetoga mogu upozoriti na svjesno i ustrajno zatvaranje pred milošću, ali bez objašnjenja mogu izazvati pretjeran strah ili navesti slušatelje da vlastite sumnje i slabosti proglase neoprostivima. Katekizam razlikuje namjerno njegovanu sumnju od nenamjerne teškoće u vjerovanju te očaj od nade u Božje oproštenje.

Suprotstavljanje „zbora pravednika” farizejskom duhu može pomoći razotkrivanju licemjerja, ali treba izbjegavati da se skupine ili protivnici opisuju kao nedostojni milosrđa. Kršćansko svjedočanstvo poziva na istinu i obraćenje, ali i na poštovanje dostojanstva svake osobe.

Domoljubna inicijativa i vjersko javno djelovanje nisu sami po sebi problematični, ali sažetak ne otkriva njihove ciljeve ni poruke. Zato ih nije moguće ocijeniti kao doprinos solidarnosti i općem dobru ili, nasuprot tome, kao instrumentalizaciju religije u političke svrhe.
overall.theological_context: Katekizam Katoličke Crkve uči da molitva izražava klanjanje, zahvaljivanje, prošnju i zagovor te vjernika osposobljava za vršenje Božjih zapovijedi; zato pobožnost krunice najbolje donosi plod kada vodi obraćenju i djelotvornoj ljubavi. Sveto pismo i crkveno tumačenje povezuju Božju pravednost s njegovom vjernom, spasenjskom milošću, pa se sud ne smije odvojiti od poziva na obraćenje i nade u oproštenje. Socijalni nauk Crkve podupire javno svjedočenje vjere i društvene inicijative koje služe općem dobru, uz poštovanje ljudskog dostojanstva i bez političke instrumentalizacije religije.

overall.assessment_en: According to the presented content, the podcast is mainly oriented toward the Gospel: it connects prayer and Christ's passion with God's mercy, conversion, and the responsible fulfillment of God's will. It is commendable that it presents Jesus not only as a merciful Savior but also as a judge; however, the formulation "without judgment there is no mercy" requires careful interpretation so that God's justice is not portrayed as contrary to mercy or as mere punishment. The emphasis on the pharisaic spirit, sin against the Holy Spirit, and perseverance can encourage a serious examination of conscience, but pastorally requires distinguishing stubborn refusal of conversion from doubt, weakness, or genuine difficulty in faith. Because public prayer, a book, and a patriotic initiative are presented only as announcements, their concrete implementation and relationship to the common good cannot be assessed from the summary.
overall.theological_context_en: The Catechism of the Catholic Church teaches that prayer expresses adoration, thanksgiving, supplication, and intercession and disposes the faithful to carry out God's commandments; therefore, devotion to the Rosary bears fruit best when it leads to conversion and effective love. Sacred Scripture and ecclesial interpretation unite God's justice with his faithful, salvific grace, so judgment must not be separated from the call to conversion and hope of forgiveness. The Social Teaching of the Church supports public witness to faith and social initiatives that serve the common good, with respect for human dignity and without political instrumentalization of religion.
seeds_of_logos_en: The Chaplet of Divine Mercy, litanies, and meditation on the sorrowful mysteries place Christ's passion and trust in God's mercy at the center of communal devotion; Christian prayer includes praise, supplication, and intercession, and should shape life rather than remain merely an outward act.

Encouragement to ask daily, "What should I do today?" connects faith with concrete moral action and the doing of God's will. This is an important anthropological emphasis: man is not merely a recipient of consolation, but a free and responsible person called to respond to God's love.

Portraying Jesus entering into conflict with the Pharisees as a call to their conversion can preserve the evangelical hope that warning is not merely condemnation: Christ's grace calls the sinner to return to God.

The call to the public Rosary can be a legitimate form of communal witness of faith and participation of the faithful in public life, provided that it respects human dignity and does not instrumentalize faith for political purposes.
concerns_en: The assertion "without judgment there is no mercy" can be theologically fruitful if it means that mercy takes seriously the truth about sin, responsibility, and conversion. It becomes risky if it suggests that judgment is primarily a threat or that God's justice and mercy are mutually exclusive: Catholic understanding connects them in God's salvific action, and the repentant sinner can rely on God's merciful justice.

The expression "when God's work is evident, there are no more excuses" and speaking about the sin against the Holy Spirit can warn against conscious and persistent closure to grace, but without explanation may provoke excessive fear or lead listeners to declare their own doubts and weaknesses unpardonable. The Catechism distinguishes deliberately cultivated doubt from involuntary difficulty in believing, and despair from hope in God's forgiveness.

Opposing the "assembly of the righteous" to the pharisaic spirit can help expose hypocrisy, but one should avoid describing groups or opponents as unworthy of mercy. Christian witness calls for truth and conversion, but also for respect for the dignity of every person.

The patriotic initiative and public religious action are not problematic in themselves, but the summary does not disclose their goals or messages. Therefore, it is not possible to evaluate them as a contribution to solidarity and the common good or, conversely, as an instrumentalization of religion for political purposes.

sections.subtitle: Sin ili vol u bunaru: evanđeoski redak dana i molitva oslobođenja
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar započinje molitvu oslobođenja i vezivanja zlih sila u ime Isusovo
sections.content:
Epizoda emisije **Ora et Labora** počinje kratkim pozdravom. Voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** pozdravlja gledatelje i slušatelje i odmah navodi evanđeoski redak dana: „Ako nekom od vas sin ili vol padne u bunar, neće li ga izvući i u dan subotnji?“ To pitanje o subotnjem spašavanju iz bunara ostaje u pozadini cijelog molitvenog dijela, a voditelj mu se vraća u nastavku emisije.

Nakon znaka križa, „U ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga“, Grebenar izgovara **molitvu oslobođenja**. U ime Isusovo „uzima vlast“ i veže sve zle sile i snage na svim mjestima koja nabraja:

- u zraku,
- na zemlji,
- u vodi,
- u podzemlju,
- na onome svijetu,
- u prirodi,
- u vatri.

Zatim ispovijeda da je Gospodin „Gospodin nad svim svemirom“ i daje mu slavu u ime njegova stvorenja. U Kristovo ime veže „sve demonske sile koje su došle protiv nas i naših obitelji“ i sve vjernike stavlja pod zaštitu **dragocjene krvi** prolivene na križu.

Molitva se nastavlja zazivom Marije. Voditelj od nje traži zaštitu i zagovor kod Presvetog Srca Isusova za sve obitelji te moli da ih „zaogrne svojim plaštem ljubavi, da se prestraši neprijatelj“. Potom zaziva **svetog Mihovila i anđele čuvare** da brane vjernike i njihove obitelji „u borbi protiv svega zla što obilazi svijetom“. Slijedi zapovijed svim silama zla da „odstupe istog časa“ od molitelja, njihovih domova i njihove zemlje. Uvodni dio završava zahvalom Isusu, koji je „vjeran Bog i osjeća s nama“.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva je pretežno usklađena s katoličkom vjerom: zaziva Božju vlast, Kristovo otkupljenje te Marijin i anđeoski zagovor, što odgovara katoličkoj molitvenoj praksi. Ipak, zapovjedni govor upućen zlim silama traži oprez jer može zvučati kao obredni egzorcizam, a opis ne razjašnjava izričito da se ne tvrdi zajamčena ili automatska zaštita.
concerns: Dio koji izravno zapovijeda silama zla da odstupe može se shvatiti kao imperativni egzorcizam. Crkveni obred razlikuje takve formule od molitve vjernika i izričito kaže da ih vjernici ne izgovaraju umjesto svećenika koji obavlja obred; stoga bi bilo dobro jasno prikazati ovu molitvu kao prošnju za Božju zaštitu, a ne kao samostalno obavljanje egzorcizma.

Izraz „veže sve zle sile” nije sam po sebi dokaz naukovne zablude, ali može sugerirati da molitelj vlastitom izjavom upravlja duhovnim silama. Katoličko shvaćanje zaštite naglašava Božje djelovanje i molitvu Crkve, a ne samostalnu ljudsku vlast nad demonima.
magisterium.enrichment: Zazivanje Marije i svetog Mihaela kao zagovornika uklapa se u molitveni jezik Crkve: službeni tekstovi mole Mariju da zagovara vjernike te traže da sveti Mihael brani ljude u duhovnoj borbi. Izraz „dragocjena krv” ima smisleno kršćansko uporište u vjeri da je Krist svojom mukom otkupio ljude; važno je, međutim, molitvu razumjeti kao pouzdanje u Boga, a ne kao formulu koja sama po sebi jamči da se zlo neće dogoditi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The prayer is predominantly aligned with the Catholic faith: it invokes God's authority, Christ's redemption, and the intercession of Mary and the angels, which corresponds to Catholic prayer practice. Nevertheless, commanding speech addressed to evil powers requires caution because it can sound like ritual exorcism, and the description does not explicitly clarify that guaranteed or automatic protection is not being claimed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Invoking Mary and Saint Michael as intercessors fits into the prayer language of the Church: official texts pray for Mary to intercede for the faithful and ask Saint Michael to defend people in spiritual warfare. The phrase "precious blood" has a meaningful Christian foundation in the faith that Christ redeemed humanity by his passion; it is important, however, to understand prayer as trust in God, rather than as a formula that of itself guarantees that evil will not happen.
concerns_en: The part that directly commands powers of evil to depart can be understood as an imperative exorcism. The Church's rite distinguishes such formulas from the prayer of the faithful and explicitly states that the faithful do not utter them in place of the priest performing the rite; therefore, it would be good to clearly present this prayer as a petition for God's protection, rather than as an independent performance of exorcism.

The phrase "binds all evil powers" is not in itself evidence of doctrinal error, but it can suggest that the one praying controls spiritual powers by their own declaration. The Catholic understanding of protection emphasizes God's action and the prayer of the Church, not independent human authority over demons.

sections.subtitle_en: Son or ox into a well: the gospel verse of the day and prayer of deliverance
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar begins the prayer of deliverance and binding of evil forces in the name of Jesus
sections.content_en:
The episode of the show **Ora et Labora** begins with a brief greeting. Host **Vladimir Grebenar** greets the viewers and listeners and immediately cites the gospel verse of the day: “If a son or ox of one of you falls into a well, will he not pull him out even on the sabbath day?” That question about sabbath rescue from a well remains in the background of the entire prayer section, and the host returns to it later in the show.

After the sign of the cross, “In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,” Grebenar speaks the **prayer of deliverance**. In the name of Jesus, he “takes authority” and binds all evil powers and forces in all the places he lists:

- in the air,
- on the earth,
- in the water,
- in the underworld,
- in the other world,
- in nature,
- in fire.

He then confesses that the Lord is “Lord over the entire universe” and gives him glory in the name of his creation. In Christ's name, he binds “all demonic forces that have come against us and our families” and places all the faithful under the protection of the **precious blood** shed on the cross.

The prayer continues with an invocation of Mary. The host asks from her protection and intercession before the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus for all families and prays that she “wrap them with her mantle of love, so that the enemy may be terrified.” Then he invokes **Saint Michael and the guardian angels** to defend the faithful and their families “in the battle against all evil that roams the world.” A command to all forces of evil follows, that they “depart this very moment” from the intercessors, their homes, and their land. The introductory section ends with thanksgiving to Jesus, who is “a faithful God and feels with us.”

sections.subtitle: Vojvoda vojske nebeske i molitva srca koja kucaju zajedno
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli molitvu jedinstva s Isusom 'Moj ljupki Isuse'
sections.content:
Iza molitve oslobođenja slijedi tradicionalna **molitva svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu**. Grebenar moli arkanđela da brani vjernike „u boju protiv pakosti i zasjeda đavolskih“ i da im bude zaklon. Arkanđela naziva „vojvodom vojske nebeske“ i moli da Sotonu i druge zle duhove, koji „svijetom obilaze na propast duša“, božanskom krepošću i jakošću strovali u pakao.

Potom ritam molitve postaje nježniji. Molitva **„Moj ljupki Isuse“** traži potpuno jedinstvo vjernika s Kristom, a to jedinstvo opisuje kroz tijelo i dušu:

- da noge zajedno hode,
- da ruke budu skupljene u jedinstvu,
- da srca kucaju zajedno,
- da duše budu u skladu,
- da misli budu kao jedno,
- da uši zajedno slušaju tišinu,
- da pogledi duboko prodru jedan u drugi,
- da usne zajedno mole.

Cilj tog sjedinjenja izrečen je na kraju: da se „zadobije milosrđe od vječnoga Oca“. Time se već u uvodu najavljuje glavna tema epizode, **Božje milosrđe**.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva svetom Mihaelu izravno odgovara tradicionalnoj molitvi koju sadrži i službeni crkveni obred, pa su zaziv anđelova zagovora i molba da Bog porazi Sotonu jasno usklađeni s katoličkom vjerom. Opis sjedinjenja s Isusom također je prihvatljiv kao pobožna slika intimnog zajedništva s Kristom, pod uvjetom da se ne shvati kao stapanje osobe s Bogom.
magisterium.enrichment: Službena molitva Crkve zaziva svetog Mihaela da brani vjernike u borbi protiv đavolskih zasjeda te ga naziva knezom nebeske vojske; opis u podcastu stoga vjerno prenosi njezin sadržaj. Katoličko sjedinjenje s Kristom znači zajedništvo života i ljubavi, a ne ukidanje razlike između Stvoritelja i stvorenja. Molba da se zadobije milosrđe Oca dobro se uklapa u kršćansku molitvu, koja milosrđe traži od Boga po Kristu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The Prayer to Saint Michael corresponds directly to the traditional prayer contained also in the official rite of the Church, so the invocation of the angel's intercession and the plea that God defeat Satan are clearly aligned with the Catholic faith. The description of union with Jesus is likewise acceptable as a pious image of intimate communion with Christ, provided it is not understood as a merging of the person with God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The official prayer of the Church invokes Saint Michael to defend the faithful in the struggle against the snares of the devil and names him prince of the heavenly host; the description in the podcast therefore faithfully conveys its content. Catholic union with Christ means a communion of life and love, not the abolition of the distinction between Creator and creature. The petition to obtain the mercy of the Father fits well into Christian prayer, which asks mercy from God through Christ.

sections.subtitle_en: The captain of the heavenly host and the prayer of hearts beating together
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays the prayer of unity with Jesus 'My lovely Jesus'
sections.content_en:
Following the prayer of deliverance comes the traditional **prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel**. Grebenar prays to the archangel to defend the faithful “in battle against the wickedness and snares of the devil” and to be their protection. He calls the archangel the “captain of the heavenly host” and prays that by the divine virtue and power he cast into hell Satan and other evil spirits who “roam through the world seeking the ruin of souls.”

Then the rhythm of prayer becomes gentler. The prayer **“My lovely Jesus”** asks for complete unity of the believer with Christ, and describes that unity through body and soul:

- that feet walk together,
- that hands be gathered in unity,
- that hearts beat together,
- that souls be in harmony,
- that thoughts be as one,
- that ears listen together to the silence,
- that gazes deeply penetrate one another,
- that lips pray together.

The goal of that union is stated at the end: to “obtain mercy from the eternal Father.” With this, already in the introduction, the main theme of the episode, the **Divine Mercy**, is announced.

sections.subtitle: Dvije posvete: Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu i Presvetom Srcu Isusovu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar izgovara posvetu Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu
sections.content:
Sljedeći dio uvodnih molitava čine dvije posvete. U **posveti Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu** voditelj predaje Djevici Mariji, „majci i kraljici“, svoje biće, misli, riječi i djela. Moli je da raspolaže njime i svime što mu pripada, „sada i u vječnosti“, na slavu Presvetoga Trojstva, za posvećenje Crkve i za spasenje svijeta.

U drugom dijelu posvete traži od Bezgrešne pomoć da živi dostojno svoga **krsnog posvećenja** i da „neopozivo pripada svome Otkupitelju“. Moli i da, poput Marije, sluša poticaje Duha Svetoga, kako bi se u njemu i u svemu vršila volja Božja.

Slijedi **molitva Presvetom Srcu Isusovu**, koje naziva „izvorom svakoga dobra“. Molitelj se tom Srcu klanja, vjeruje mu, ufa se u njega, ljubi ga i kaje se za svoje grijehe. Isusu poklanja svoje „siromašno srce“ i moli da ga učini:

- **poniznim**,
- **strpljivim**,
- **čistim**,
- sukladnim Isusovim željama.

Molitva traži i da molitelj živi u Isusu i Isus u njemu, zaštitu u opasnostima te utjehu u nevoljama i žalostima. Završava molbom za zdravlje tijela, blagoslov rada i milost dobre smrti.

magisterium.assessment: Opis posvete Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu i molitve Presvetom Srcu Isusovu uglavnom je jasno usklađen s katoličkom pobožnošću: Marijina se uloga prikazuje u službi Presvetoga Trojstva, Crkve i spasenja, a Isus ostaje Otkupitelj i središte molitve. Povezivanje Srca Marijina i Srca Isusova odgovara crkvenom nauku, uz važnu razliku između Krista, pravoga Boga, i Marije, stvorenja i učenice svoga Sina.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička posveta Mariji ne znači štovanje koje pripada Bogu niti zamjenjuje krsno pripadanje Kristu; ovdje se moli da Marija pomogne živjeti krsno posvećenje i vršiti Božju volju. Crkva vidi njezino Bezgrešno Srce kao povezano sa Sinovim djelom spasenja, ali istodobno čuva „nepremostivu udaljenost” između Sina, koji je pravi Bog, i Majke, koja je stvorenje.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary and the prayer to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus is mainly clearly aligned with Catholic devotion: Mary's role is presented in the service of the Most Holy Trinity, the Church, and salvation, while Jesus remains the Redeemer and the center of prayer. Connecting the Heart of Mary and the Heart of Jesus corresponds to ecclesial teaching, with an important distinction between Christ, true God, and Mary, a creature and disciple of her Son.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic consecration to Mary does not mean the worship that belongs to God, nor does it replace baptismal belonging to Christ; here it is prayed that Mary may help in living baptismal consecration and doing God's will. The Church sees her Immaculate Heart as united with the Son's work of salvation, but at the same time preserves the "infinite distance" between the Son, who is true God, and the Mother, who is a creature.

sections.subtitle_en: Two consecrations: to the Immaculate Heart of Mary and to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar speaks the consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary
sections.content_en:
The next part of the introductory prayers consists of two consecrations. In the **consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary**, the host surrenders to the Virgin Mary, “mother and queen,” his being, thoughts, words, and deeds. He asks her to dispose of him and all that belongs to him, “now and in eternity,” for the glory of the Most Holy Trinity, for the sanctification of the Church, and for the salvation of the world.

In the second part of the consecration, he asks the Immaculate One for help to live worthily his **baptismal consecration** and to “irrevocably belong to his Redeemer.” He also prays that, like Mary, he listen to the promptings of the Holy Spirit, so that in him and in all things the will of God may be done.

There follows the **prayer to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus**, which he calls the “source of every good.” The petitioner adores this Heart, believes in it, hopes in it, loves it, and repents for his sins. To Jesus he offers his “poor heart” and prays that he make it:

- **humble**,
- **patient**,
- **pure**,
- conforming to Jesus's desires.

The prayer also asks that the petitioner live in Jesus and Jesus in him, for protection in dangers, and comfort in troubles and sorrows. It concludes with a petition for bodily health, a blessing on work, and the grace of a happy death.

sections.subtitle: Krunica Božjega milosrđa: „Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli 'Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv' na početku desetice krunice Božjeg milosrđa
sections.content:
U 00:03:42 Grebenar najavljuje **Krunicu Božjega milosrđa**, središnju molitvu epizode posvećene temi milosrđa. Uvodne molitve su Oče naš, Zdravo Marijo i Apostolsko vjerovanje, koje voditelj izgovara cijelo, od Boga Oca Stvoritelja do „uskrsnuća tijela i života vječnoga“.

Slijedi pet desetica. Svaka počinje prikazanjem:

> „Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv, dušu i božanstvo preljubljenoga Sina tvojega, Gospodina našega Isusa Krista, kao zadovoljštinu za grijehe naše i cijeloga svijeta.“

Iza prikazanja deset se puta ponavlja kratki zaziv: **„Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci, budi milosrdan nama i cijelome svijetu.“** Ponavljanje traje gotovo šest i pol minuta i daje molitvi meditativan ritam. Isti zaziv vraća se iz desetice u deseticu, a u njegovu je središtu Kristova muka kao temelj milosrđa za cijeli svijet.

Krunica završava trostrukim zazivom **„Sveti Bože, sveti jaki Bože, sveti besmrtni Bože, smiluj se nama i cijelomu svijetu“**. Iza njega dolazi molitva krvi i vodi „što potekoste iz Srca Isusova kao izvor milosrđa za nas“, zaziv „Marijo, majko milosrđa, moli za nas“ te tri puta ponovljeno **„Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“**.

magisterium.assessment: Krunica Božjega milosrđa usmjerava molitvu na Kristovu muku kao izvor oproštenja i milosrđa, a zazivi za cijeli svijet izražavaju univerzalnu otvorenost Kristova otkupiteljskog djela. Molitva je u skladu s biblijskim naukom da je Kristovo tijelo predano i krv prolivena za oproštenje grijeha te da je on pomirnica ne samo za naše grijehe nego i za grijehe svega svijeta.
magisterium.enrichment: Izraz „kao zadovoljštinu” treba razumjeti úgy da se molitva vjernika sjedinjuje s Kristovim jedinom jačom otkupiteljskom žrtvom, a ne da joj nešto nedostaje ili da je ponavlja kao novu žrtvu. Crkveni nauk naglašava da sva vrijednost zadovoljštine izvire iz Kristove žrtve, koja se sakramentalno uprisutnjuje u euharistiji, dok vjernici mogu prikazivati svoje molitve i život u sjedinjenju s njim.
magisterium.assessment_en: The Chaplet of Divine Mercy directs prayer to Christ's passion as the source of forgiveness and mercy, and invocations for the whole world express the universal openness of Christ's redemptive work. The prayer is in accordance with the biblical teaching that Christ's body was given and blood shed for the forgiveness of sins, and that he is the expiation not only for our sins but also for the sins of the whole world.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The phrase "in atonement" should be understood such that the prayer of the faithful is united with Christ's uniquely efficacious redemptive sacrifice, and not that anything is lacking in it or that it repeats it as a new sacrifice. Church teaching emphasizes that all value of atonement flows from Christ's sacrifice, which is made sacramentally present in the Eucharist, while the faithful may offer their prayers and life in union with him.

sections.subtitle_en: The Chaplet of the Divine Mercy: “For the sake of his sorrowful Passion”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays 'Eternal Father, we offer you the body and blood' at the beginning of a decade of the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy
sections.content_en:
At 00:03:42 Grebenar announces the **Chaplet of the Divine Mercy**, the central prayer of the episode dedicated to the theme of mercy. The introductory prayers are the Our Father, Hail Mary, and the Apostles' Creed, which the host recites in full, from God the Father Creator to the “resurrection of the body and life everlasting.”

Five decades follow. Each begins with the offering:

> “Eternal Father, we offer you the body and blood, soul and divinity of your dearly beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, in atonement for our sins and those of the whole world.”

Following the offering, a short invocation is repeated ten times: **“For the sake of his sorrowful Passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world.”** The repetition lasts almost six and a half minutes and gives the prayer a meditative rhythm. The same invocation returns from decade to decade, and at its center is Christ's Passion as the foundation of mercy for the whole world.

The Chaplet concludes with the threefold invocation **“Holy God, Holy Mighty One, Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us and on the whole world”**. Following it comes the prayer to the blood and water “which gushed forth from the Heart of Jesus as a fount of mercy for us,” the invocation “Mary, mother of mercy, pray for us,” and the three times repeated **“Jesus, I trust in you”**.

sections.subtitle: Litanije Božjem milosrđu: od stvaranja do duša u čistilištu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar moli zazive 'Milosrđe Božje, uzdam se u tebe'

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom snažno usklađen s katoličkom vjerom: pouzdanje u Božje milosrđe prikazuje u povezanosti s Kristom, Presvetim Trojstvom, Crkvom i sakramentima, bez vidljive tvrdnje koja bi proturječila nauku. Posebno je važno razumjeti te zazive kao pobožnu molitvu, a ne kao obećanje da će pouzdanje samo po sebi ukloniti svaku patnju ili zamijeniti obraćenje i sakramentalni život.
concerns: Formulacije da milosrđe „čuva od paklenoga ognja” i olakšava patnje dušama u čistilištu treba čitati kao prošnju i izraz nade u Božje milosrđe, a ne kao automatsko jamstvo spasenja ili tvrdnju da molitva uklanja potrebu za osobnim obraćenjem.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička pobožnost Božjem milosrđu usmjerena je na milosrđe objavljeno u Kristovoj smrti i uskrsnuću te na oproštenje grijeha i obnovu života. Crkva stoga potiče da se ta pobožnost razumije u svjetlu liturgije; milosrđe se u sakramentalnom životu ne samo zaziva nego i prima, osobito u sakramentima pomirenja i euharistije.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly strongly aligned with the Catholic faith: it presents trust in God's mercy in connection with Christ, the Most Holy Trinity, the Church, and the sacraments, without any apparent claim contradicting doctrine. It is especially important to understand these invocations as pious prayer, and not as a promise that trust in itself will remove all suffering or replace conversion and sacramental life.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic devotion to Divine Mercy is directed toward the mercy revealed in Christ's death and resurrection and toward the forgiveness of sins and the renewal of life. The Church therefore encourages this devotion to be understood in the light of the liturgy; in sacramental life, mercy is not only invoked but also received, especially in the sacraments of reconciliation and the Eucharist.
concerns_en: Formulations that mercy "protects from the fire of hell" and relieves sufferings of souls in purgatory should be read as supplication and an expression of hope in God's mercy, and not as an automatic guarantee of salvation or a claim that prayer removes the need for personal conversion.

sections.subtitle: Gospina krunica: Getsemanski krvavi znoj i bičevanje
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje prvo otajstvo Gospine krunice: 'koji je za nas krvavim znojem znojio'
sections.content:
Nakon molitava Božjem milosrđu Grebenar najavljuje: „Slijedi Gospina krunica.“ Mole se **žalosna otajstva**, koja prate Kristovu muku od Maslinske gore do Kalvarije.

Svako otajstvo ima isti raspored:

- najava otajstva,
- molitva **Oče naš**,
- deset **Zdravo Marija**,
- **Slava Ocu**,
- zaziv „O moj Isuse, oprosti nam naše grijehe, očuvaj nas od paklenoga ognja, dovedi u raj sve duše, a osobito one kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe“.

Završni zaziv svake desetice ponovno spominje milosrđe i tako povezuje Gospinu krunicu s prethodnom krunicom i litanijama.

**Prvo otajstvo**, „koji je za nas krvavim znojem znojio“, počinje u 00:16:40. Posvećeno je Isusovoj tjeskobi u molitvi pred muku.

**Drugo otajstvo**, „koji je za nas bio bičevan“, započinje oko 00:20:30. Voditelj moli mirnim i ujednačenim tempom, a ponavljanje anđeoskog pozdrava daje vrijeme za razmatranje Kristove patnje.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je jasno usklađen s katoličkom vjerom i Svetim pismom: žalosna otajstva razmatraju Kristovu muku, počevši od njegove tjeskobne molitve u Getsemaniju i završavajući putem prema Kalvariji. Ustroj desetice i zaziv „O moj Isuse” prikazani su kao pobožni način molitve i razmatranja, bez naznake da bi zamjenjivali liturgiju ili Kristovo jedinstveno djelo spasenja.
magisterium.enrichment: U Getsemaniju Isus moli da se vrši Očeva volja, a razmatranje krunice pomaže vjerniku promatrati tu poslušnost i ljubav u svjetlu cijele muke. Ivanovo evanđelje izričito spominje da je Pilat dao Isusa bičevati; papa Ivan Pavao II. objašnjava da žalosna otajstva vode prema središtu Božje ljubavi i izvoru našega spasenja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is clearly aligned with the Catholic faith and Sacred Scripture: the sorrowful mysteries meditate on Christ's passion, beginning with his agony in Gethsemane and concluding with the way toward Calvary. The structure of the decade and the invocation "O my Jesus" are presented as a pious way of prayer and meditation, with no indication that they would replace the liturgy or Christ's unique work of salvation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Gethsemane Jesus prays that the Father's will be done, and meditation on the Rosary helps the believer contemplate that obedience and love in the light of the entire passion. The Gospel of John explicitly mentions that Pilate had Jesus scourged; Pope John Paul II explains that the sorrowful mysteries lead toward the center of God's love and the source of our salvation.

sections.subtitle_en: Our Lady's Rosary: Gethsemane bloody sweat and the scourging
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the first mystery of Our Lady's Rosary: 'who sweated bloody sweat for us'
sections.content_en:
After the prayers to the Divine Mercy, Grebenar announces: “Our Lady's Rosary follows.” The **sorrowful mysteries** are prayed, tracing Christ's Passion from the Mount of Olives to Calvary.

Each mystery has the same structure:

- announcement of the mystery,
- the **Our Father** prayer,
- ten **Hail Marys**,
- the **Glory Be**,
- the invocation “O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell, lead all souls to heaven, especially those in most need of your mercy.”

The closing invocation of each decade mentions mercy once again, thus linking Our Lady's Rosary with the preceding chaplet and litany.

The **first mystery**, “who sweated bloody sweat for us,” begins at 00:16:40. It is dedicated to Jesus's agony in prayer before the Passion.

The **second mystery**, “who was scourged for us,” begins around 00:20:30. The host prays at a calm and steady pace, and the repetition of the angelic salutation provides time for meditating on Christ's suffering.

sections.subtitle: Kruna od trnja, teški križ i raspeće
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje peto otajstvo: 'koji je za nas bio razapet'
sections.content:
Druga polovica Gospine krunice prati vrhunac Kristove muke.

**Treće otajstvo**, „koji je za nas trnjem bio okrunjen“, voditelj najavljuje u 00:24:27. Slijede Oče naš, deset Zdravo Marija, Slava Ocu i zaziv za oproštenje grijeha i za duše kojima je najpotrebnije milosrđe.

**Četvrto otajstvo**, „koji je za nas teški križ nosio“, počinje u 00:28:23 i posvećeno je Kristovu putu prema Kalvariji.

**Peto otajstvo**, „koji je za nas bio razapet“, započinje u 00:32:21 i završava krunicu. Molitelj ovdje razmatra raspeće, koje se u ovoj epizodi više puta spominje kao izvor milosrđa. Isti motiv javlja se i u molitvi oslobođenja, u zazivu Kristove krvi „prolivene za nas na križu“, i u Krunici Božjega milosrđa, u riječima o „pregorkoj muci“.

Nakon svake desetice ponavlja se ista molba: oproštenje grijeha, očuvanje od paklenoga ognja i spasenje svih duša, „a osobito onih kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe“.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz žalosnih otajstava u skladu je s katoličkim naukom: krunica usmjerava razmatranje na Kristovu muku, a njegovo trpljenje i smrt na križu prikazuje kao objavu Božje ljubavi i izvor spasenja. Molitva za oproštenje grijeha i za duše kojima je najpotrebnije milosrđe izražava prošnju i zagovor, a ne tvrdnju da će se svi nužno spasiti.
magisterium.enrichment: Razmatranje krunjenja trnjem, nošenja križa i raspeća nije samo prisjećanje na povijesne događaje: prema učenju Ivana Pavla II., žalosna otajstva pozivaju vjernike da uđu u dubinu Božje ljubavi i dožive njezinu životvornu snagu. Kristova poslušnost Očevoj volji i njegova smrt na križu središte su tog razmatranja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The presentation of the sorrowful mysteries is in accordance with Catholic teaching: the Rosary directs meditation to Christ's passion, and presents his suffering and death on the cross as a revelation of God's love and the source of salvation. Prayer for the forgiveness of sins and for souls most in need of mercy expresses supplication and intercession, not a claim that all will necessarily be saved.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Meditation on the crowning with thorns, carrying of the cross, and crucifixion is not merely a recollection of historical events: according to the teaching of John Paul II, the sorrowful mysteries invite the faithful to enter into the depth of God's love and experience its life-giving power. Christ's obedience to the Father's will and his death on the cross are the center of that meditation.

sections.subtitle_en: The crown of thorns, the heavy cross, and the crucifixion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar announces the fifth mystery: 'who was crucified for us'
sections.content_en:
The second half of Our Lady's Rosary traces the culmination of Christ's Passion.

The **third mystery**, “who was crowned with thorns for us,” is announced by the host at 00:24:27. There follow the Our Father, ten Hail Marys, the Glory Be, and the invocation for forgiveness of sins and for souls in most need of mercy.

The **fourth mystery**, “who carried the heavy cross for us,” begins at 00:28:23 and is dedicated to Christ's way toward Calvary.

The **fifth mystery**, “who was crucified for us,” begins at 00:32:21 and concludes the rosary. Here the petitioner contemplates the crucifixion, which in this episode is mentioned multiple times as the source of mercy. The same motif appears also in the prayer of deliverance, in the invocation of Christ's blood “shed for us on the cross,” and in the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy, in the words about the “sorrowful Passion.”

After each decade the same petition is repeated: forgiveness of sins, preservation from the fire of hell, and salvation of all souls, “especially those who are in most need of your mercy.”

sections.subtitle: „Zdravo, Kraljice“: vapaj prognanih sinova Evinih
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli završnu marijansku molitvu 'Zdravo Kraljice'
sections.content:
Molitveni dio završava antifonom **„Zdravo, Kraljice“**. Mariju se pozdravlja kao **„majku milosrđa“**, „život, slast i ufanje naše“, pa se tema milosrđa javlja i u posljednjoj molitvi ovog dijela.

Vjernici joj se obraćaju kao „prognani sinovi Evini“ i uzdišu „tugujući i plačući u ovoj suznoj dolini“. Mole Mariju, kao svoju zagovornicu, da na njih svrne svoje milostive oči i da im „poslije ovoga progona“ pokaže Isusa, „blagoslovljeni plod utrobe svoje“.

Molitva završava zazivom „O blaga, o mila, o slatka Djevice Marijo“. Time se zaokružuje molitveni dio emisije, koji je počeo molitvom oslobođenja, nastavio se krunicom i litanijama Božjem milosrđu te razmatranjem Kristove muke kroz žalosna otajstva. Nakon toga Vladimir Grebenar prelazi na tumačenje Svetoga pisma.

magisterium.assessment: Opis molitve „Zdravo, Kraljice“ i njezinih zaziva Mariji kao majci milosrđa i zagovornici u skladu je s katoličkom pobožnošću, kako je prikazana u odlomku. Ne prikazuje Mariju kao zamjenu za Krista: završni vapaj moli da ona vjernicima pokaže Isusa, dok katoličko razmatranje Kristove muke Mariju smješta uz njezina Sina pod križem.
magisterium.enrichment: Izraz „prognani sinovi Evini“ i slika „suzne doline“ pjesnički opisuju ljudsku ranjenost, grijeh i zemaljsko hodočašće; nisu tvrdnja da je zemaljski život bez ikakva dobra ili da je Marija izvor spasenja neovisno o Kristu. U katoličkom razumijevanju Marijino majčinstvo i zagovor usmjereni su prema Kristu: Ivan Pavao II. opisuje vjernike kako s Marijom stoje pod križem i ulaze u dubinu Božje ljubavi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the prayer "Hail, Holy Queen" and its invocations to Mary as mother of mercy and intercessor is in accordance with Catholic devotion, as presented in the passage. It does not present Mary as a substitute for Christ: the final cry prays that she show Jesus to the faithful, while Catholic meditation on Christ's passion places Mary beside her Son beneath the cross.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The expression "banished children of Eve" and the image "valley of tears" poetically describe human woundedness, sin, and earthly pilgrimage; they are not an assertion that earthly life is devoid of any good or that Mary is the source of salvation independently of Christ. In Catholic understanding, Mary's motherhood and intercession are directed toward Christ: John Paul II describes the faithful as standing with Mary beneath the cross and entering into the depth of God's love.

sections.subtitle_en: “Hail, Holy Queen”: the cry of the banished children of Eve
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays the concluding Marian prayer 'Hail, Holy Queen'
sections.content_en:
The prayer section concludes with the antiphon **“Hail, Holy Queen”**. Mary is greeted as the **“mother of mercy”**, “our life, our sweetness, and our hope,” so the theme of mercy appears in the final prayer of this section as well.

The faithful address her as “poor banished children of Eve” and sigh, “mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.” They ask Mary, as their advocate, to turn her eyes of mercy toward them and, “after this our exile,” to show them Jesus, “the blessed fruit of thy womb.”

The prayer concludes with the invocation “O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.” This rounds out the prayer section of the show, which began with the prayer of deliverance, continued with the chaplet and litany of the Divine Mercy, and the meditation on Christ's Passion through the sorrowful mysteries. After that, Vladimir Grebenar moves on to the exposition of the Holy Scriptures.

sections.subtitle: Kratka zabuna na početku tumačenja: umjesto Efežanima, Poslanica Filipljanima
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Vladimir Grebenar ispričava se gledateljima jer mu se otvorio pogrešan biblijski tekst
sections.content:
Nakon završene Krunice Božjega milosrđa, Gospine krunice i molitve *Zdravo, Kraljice*, voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** prelazi na središnji dio emisije, tumačenje svete riječi. Najavljuje čitanje iz Poslanice Efežanima i izgovara prve riječi: „Braćo, podložni budite jedni drugima u strahu Kristovu.“

Nakon kratke stanke slijedi ispravak. Grebenar se gledateljima i slušateljima jednostavno ispričava jer mu se otvorio krivi tekst. Pravo čitanje toga dana je **Poslanica Filipljanima**.

Zatim čita uvodni pozdrav apostola Pavla i Timoteja, „sluga Krista Isusa“, upućen svima svetima u Filipima, zajedno s nadglednicima i poslužiteljima. Pavao zahvaljuje Bogu kad god se sjeti te zajednice i za nju se raduje u molitvi zbog njezina udjela u evanđelju „od onoga prvoga dana sve do sada“. Izražava i čvrsto uvjerenje da će onaj koji je u njima započeo dobro djelo to djelo dovršiti „do dana Krista Isusa“.

Tekst završava Pavlovom molitvom da ljubav vjernika sve više raste u spoznaji i potpunom pronicanju. Tako bi mogli prosuditi što je najbolje i biti „čisti i besprijekorni za dan Kristov, puni ploda pravednosti po Isusu Kristu na slavu i hvalu Božju“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu sa Svetim pismom: nakon što je ispravljena početna zamjena poslanica, sažetak vjerno prenosi pozdrav Pavla i Timoteja te Pavlovu zahvalnost, molitvu i nadu da će Bog dovršiti započeto dobro djelo. Završni naglasak na rastu ljubavi, razlučivanju dobra i plodovima pravednosti odgovara Fil 1,1–11.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavlova molitva povezuje ljubav s „spoznajom i potpunim pronicanjem“: kršćanska ljubav nije samo osjećaj, nego uključuje razborito razlučivanje i život koji donosi plodove po Kristu. Izraz „dan Kristov“ u odlomku usmjerava zajednicu prema konačnom susretu s Gospodinom, dok pouzdanje da Bog dovršava započeto dobro djelo nije poziv na pasivnost, nego temelj nade i vjernosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Sacred Scripture: after the initial mix-up of epistles was corrected, the summary faithfully conveys the greeting of Paul and Timothy as well as Paul's thanksgiving, prayer, and hope that God will complete the good work begun. The final emphasis on the growth of love, discernment of good, and fruits of righteousness corresponds to Phil 1:1–11.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul's prayer connects love with "knowledge and all discernment": Christian love is not merely a feeling, but includes prudent discernment and a life that bears fruit through Christ. The expression "day of Christ" in the passage directs the community toward the definitive encounter with the Lord, while confidence that God completes the good work begun is not a call to passivity, but the foundation of hope and fidelity.

sections.subtitle_en: Brief confusion at the beginning of the exposition: instead of Ephesians, the Epistle to the Philippians
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Vladimir Grebenar apologizes to the viewers because the wrong biblical text opened for him
sections.content_en:
After concluding the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy, Our Lady's Rosary, and the prayer *Hail, Holy Queen*, host **Vladimir Grebenar** proceeds to the central part of the show, the exposition of the holy word. He announces the reading from the Epistle to the Ephesians and recites the first words: “Brethren, be subject to one another in the fear of Christ.”

After a brief pause, a correction follows. Grebenar simply apologizes to the viewers and listeners because the wrong text had opened for him. The true reading of that day is the **Epistle to the Philippians**.

Then he reads the introductory greeting of the apostles Paul and Timothy, “servants of Christ Jesus,” addressed to all the saints in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons. Paul thanks God whenever he remembers that community and rejoices for it in prayer because of its partnership in the gospel “from the first day until now.” He also expresses a firm conviction that he who began a good work in them will bring it to completion “until the day of Christ Jesus.”

The text concludes with Paul's prayer that the love of the believers may abound more and more in knowledge and all discernment. In this way they might approve what is best and be “pure and blameless for the day of Christ, filled with the fruit of righteousness through Jesus Christ to the glory and praise of God.”

sections.subtitle: „Ono što je u srcu, to na usta izlazi“ – Dan Kristov upisan u Božji kalendar
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava da Dan Kristov ne postoji u svjetovnom kalendaru, nego u Božjem
sections.content:
Grebenar iz pročitanog teksta izvlači **dvije ključne duhovne poruke**.

Prva se tiče samog apostola. Sveti Pavao gotovo u svakoj rečenici spominje Isusa Krista. Voditelj to sažima riječima: „Puna usta Isusa. Zašto? Pa puno srce Isusa. Ono što je u srcu, to na usta izlazi.“ Pavlovo neprestano spominjanje Krista, Gospodina, Boga i Oca za njega je izraz srca ispunjena ljubavlju prema Kristu Isusu.

Druga poruka odnosi se na **Dan Kristov**. Grebenar napominje da se taj dan u tekstu piše velikim slovom i spominje više puta. Pavao njime priprema i opominje zajednicu u Filipima da se spremi za taj dan. Voditelj zatim postavlja pitanje: „Koji je to dan, braćo i sestre? Ima li ga u kalendaru?“

Odgovara da ga u svjetovnom, zemaljskom kalendaru ne poznajemo, ali je **upisan u Božji kalendar**. Bog za svakoga zna kada će napustiti ovaj svijet. Za pojedinca je Dan Kristov prije svega osobni susret s Isusom, **prvi sud**.

Postoji, međutim, i drugi Dan Kristov koji se odnosi na čitav svijet. To je dan kada Isus sudi narode.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da govor može odražavati ono što čovjek nosi u srcu dobro je u skladu s evanđeoskom poukom, a katolička vjera potvrđuje i osobni sud nakon smrti i opći sud pri Kristovu slavnom dolasku. Ipak, odlomak je neprecizan kada ih prikazuje kao dva odvojena „Dana Kristova“: osobni sud nastupa nakon smrti, dok se izraz „Dan Kristov“ u Fil 1,6.10 odnosi na dovršenje Božjeg djela i očekivanje Kristova dolaska, pa bi trebalo jasnije razlikovati te događaje.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je Dan Kristov za pojedinca „prije svega“ osobni susret i prvi sud može zamagliti razliku između osobnog suda nakon smrti i općeg suda na kraju vremena; nije precizno govoriti o njima kao o dva zasebna Dana Kristova.
Izraz „sud nad narodima“ može se razumjeti kao sud nad svim ljudima okupljenima pred Kristom, a ne samo kao zasebna osuda političkih naroda.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk razlikuje osobni sud, na kojem se nakon smrti očituje čovjekov odnos prema Bogu, od općeg suda, kada će se Krist vratiti u slavi i pred svima očitovati konačni smisao ljudskih djela i povijesti. Katekizam ističe da će se na posljednjem sudu razotkriti ponašanje i tajne srca te da će se odnos prema bližnjemu pokazati kao prihvaćanje ili odbijanje Božje ljubavi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that speech can reflect what man carries in his heart accords well with Gospel instruction, and the Catholic faith affirms both the particular judgment after death and the general judgment at Christ's glorious coming. Nevertheless, the passage is imprecise when it portrays them as two separate "Days of Christ": the particular judgment occurs after death, while the expression "Day of Christ" in Phil 1:6, 10 refers to the completion of God's work and the expectation of Christ's coming, so these events should be distinguished more clearly.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching distinguishes the particular judgment, in which man's relationship with God is manifested after death, from the general judgment, when Christ will return in glory and reveal before all the ultimate meaning of human deeds and history. The Catechism points out that at the final judgment conduct and the secrets of hearts will be revealed, and that one's relationship to neighbor will show itself as acceptance or rejection of God's love.
concerns_en: The claim that the Day of Christ for an individual is "above all" a personal encounter and first judgment can obscure the distinction between the particular judgment after death and the general judgment at the end of time; it is not precise to speak of them as two separate Days of Christ.
The phrase "judgment over the nations" can be understood as judgment over all people gathered before Christ, rather than merely as a separate condemnation of political nations.

sections.subtitle_en: “Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks” – The Day of Christ written into God's calendar
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains that the Day of Christ does not exist on the worldly calendar, but on God's
sections.content_en:
Grebenar draws **two key spiritual messages** from the reading.

The first concerns the apostle himself. Saint Paul mentions Jesus Christ in almost every sentence. The host summarizes this with the words: “Mouth full of Jesus. Why? Because the heart is full of Jesus. Out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.” Paul's unceasing mention of Christ, the Lord, God, and the Father is for him an expression of a heart filled with love toward Christ Jesus.

The second message relates to the **Day of Christ**. Grebenar notes that this day is capitalized in the text and mentioned multiple times. With it, Paul prepares and admonishes the community in Philippi to prepare for that day. The host then poses the question: “What day is that, brothers and sisters? Is it on the calendar?”

He answers that on the worldly, earthly calendar we do not know it, but it is **written into God's calendar**. God knows for everyone when they will leave this world. For the individual, the Day of Christ is first and foremost a personal encounter with Jesus, the **particular judgment**.

There exists, however, another Day of Christ that pertains to the whole world. That is the day when Jesus judges the nations.

sections.subtitle: Bez suda nema milosrđa: Isus nije samo milosrdni Spasitelj nego i sudac
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj naglašava da su sud i milosrđe dvije strane iste kovanice
sections.content:
U ovom dijelu tumačenja Grebenar ispravlja, kako ga vidi, jednostrano poimanje Krista. „Mnogi vide Isusa samo kao milosrdnog spasitelja. No Isus je i sudac, braćo i sestre“, ističe.

Svoju tvrdnju obrazlaže jednostavnom logikom: milosrđe ne može iskazati onaj tko nema vlast suditi.

- „Samo sudac može iskazati milosrđe.“
- „Samo onaj koji sudi može iskazati milosrđe.“
- „Bez suda nema milosrđa.“

Sud i milosrđe voditelj opisuje kao **dva naličja jedne kovanice**, toliko povezana da jedno bez drugoga nema smisla. Isus je, prema njegovim riječima, milosrdni Bog kako se objavio svetici Faustini Kovalskoj, ali istodobno i **strogi sudac**. Dan Kristov zato je dan suda.

Iz toga slijedi poziv vjernicima. Na taj se dan treba pripremati tako da im Bog otvori vrata milosrđa i kaže: „Ovi su moji, ove ne sudim.“ Ovaj dio tumačenja izravno se nadovezuje na naslov epizode, *Milosrđe Božje – Dan velikoga suda!*.

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno je naglašeno da je Krist sudac živih i mrtvih te da se njegovo milosrđe ne smije odvajati od istine, obraćenja i konačnog suda. Ipak, tvrdnja „bez suda nema milosrđa” izrečena je previše kategorično: milosrđe nije moguće svesti na čin suca, a povoljna presuda nije isto što i izostanak suda.
concerns: Logika „samo sudac može iskazati milosrđe” nije precizna kao opća tvrdnja: i ljudi koji nisu suci mogu biti milosrdni, a Božje milosrđe nije ovisno o tome da Bog prethodno osudi ili kazni.
Izraz „Ove ne sudim” može ostaviti pogrešan dojam da pravednici neće biti podvrgnuti sudu. Katolički nauk govori o sudu svih ljudi, ali Kristov sud može biti povoljan i usmjeren prema spasenju.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk drži zajedno obje istine: Krist ima puno pravo konačno suditi ljudska djela i srca, a Sin je došao spasiti i dati život; odbacivanje ponuđene milosti može čovjeka dovesti do samoosude. Zato je bolje reći da Kristovo milosrđe ne ukida sud, nego se u njegovu spasenjskom djelu očituje zajedno s pravednošću.
magisterium.assessment_en: It is correctly emphasized that Christ is the judge of the living and the dead and that his mercy must not be separated from truth, conversion, and final judgment. Nevertheless, the claim "without judgment there is no mercy" is stated too categorically: mercy cannot be reduced to the act of a judge, and a favorable verdict is not the same as the absence of judgment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Ecclesial teaching holds both truths together: Christ has the full right definitively to judge human deeds and hearts, and the Son came to save and give life; rejection of offered grace can lead a person to self-condemnation. Therefore, it is better to say that Christ's mercy does not abolish judgment, but is manifested in his salvific work together with righteousness.
concerns_en: The logic that "only a judge can show mercy" is not precise as a general claim: people who are not judges can also be merciful, and God's mercy is not dependent on God previously condemning or punishing.

The expression "These I do not judge" can leave the false impression that the righteous will not be subjected to judgment. Catholic teaching speaks of the judgment of all people, but Christ's judgment can be favorable and directed toward salvation.

sections.subtitle_en: Without judgment there is no mercy: Jesus is not only a merciful Savior but also a judge
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host emphasizes that judgment and mercy are two sides of the same coin
sections.content_en:
In this part of the exposition, Grebenar corrects what he sees as a one-sided understanding of Christ. “Many see Jesus only as a merciful savior. But Jesus is also a judge, brothers and sisters,” he stresses.

He supports his claim with simple logic: one who has no authority to judge cannot show mercy.

- “Only a judge can show mercy.”
- “Only the one who judges can show mercy.”
- “Without judgment there is no mercy.”

The host describes judgment and mercy as **two sides of one coin**, so linked that one without the other has no meaning. Jesus is, according to his words, a merciful God as he revealed himself to Saint Faustina Kowalska, but at the same time a **strict judge**. The Day of Christ is therefore a day of judgment.

From this follows a call to the faithful. One should prepare for that day so that God opens the door of mercy to them and says: “These are mine, these I do not judge.” This part of the exposition connects directly to the title of the episode, *God's Mercy – The Day of the Great Judgment!*.

sections.subtitle: Hvaliti Boga u zboru pravednika, a ne samo podizanjem ruku
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar upozorava da zajednicu pravednika ne čine oni koji samo dižu ruke i pjevaju, nego oni koji vrše volju Božju
sections.content:
Slijedi čitanje psalma: „Hvalit ću Gospodina svim srcem svojim u zboru pravednika, u zajednici njihovoj. Silna su djela Gospodnja…“ Psalam dalje veliča Gospodina koji je milostiv i milosrdan, koji daje hranu svojim štovateljima i dovijeka se sjeća svoga saveza.

Grebenar se zadržava na **prvom retku** i pita kako treba hvaliti Gospodina. Odgovor nalazi u samom tekstu: svim srcem, i to u **zboru pravednika**, dakle među onima koji vrše volju Božju. Smatra da bi nad tim retkom trebalo duže meditirati te pita tko je doživio da svim srcem kliče, pjeva i slavi Boga upravo u zajednici ljudi koji vrše Božju volju.

Zatim, kako sam kaže, postaje „vrlo konkretan“. Zbor pravednika nije zajednica ljudi koji samo dižu ruke u zrak i pjevaju Bogu. Ima onih koji dižu ruke, pjevaju, mole, pa i mole u jezicima, a ne vrše volju Božju.

Kao potvrdu navodi Isusove riječi: „Neće svaki koji mi govori: Gospodine, Gospodine, ući u kraljevstvo Božje, već oni koji vrše volju Oca mojega koji je na nebesima.“ Podsjeća i na nastavak, u kojem mnogi u onaj dan govore da su u Isusovo ime prorokovali i izgonili zle duhove, a on im odgovara: „Odlazite od mene, bezakonici.“

Zaključuje da su mnogi slavili Boga, ali nisu živjeli po njegovoj volji. Nisu prokazivali zlo i bili su bezakonici. Upravo zato psalam izričito govori o zboru pravednika.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje dobro povezuje psalam o hvaljenju Boga u zajednici pravednih s Isusovim upozorenjem da samo izgovaranje „Gospodine, Gospodine” ne jamči ulazak u Kraljevstvo, nego je potrebno vršiti Očevu volju. Upozorenje je u skladu s biblijskim tekstovima, uz napomenu da ono ne znači kako su molitva, pjesma ili karizmatski darovi sami po sebi bezvrijedni.
concerns: Suprotstavljanje vršenja Božje volje podizanju ruku, pjevanju i molitvi može se pogrešno shvatiti kao omalovažavanje tih oblika bogoslužja; problem je njihovo odvajanje od obraćenog života, a ne sama molitvena gesta.
Zaključak da bezakonici „nisu prokazivali zlo” nije izravno naveden u citiranom odlomku Matejeva evanđelja, koji naglašava vršenje Očeve volje.
magisterium.enrichment: Psalam 111 povezuje hvalu cijelim srcem sa zajednicom čestitih, Božjim savezom i prakticiranjem njegovih zapovijedi, pa se hvaljenje ne svodi na osjećaj ili vanjsku gestu. Isusovo upozorenje usmjerava vjernika na cjelovitost: molitva i karizme trebaju biti povezane s poslušnošću Bogu i životom koji odgovara njegovoj volji.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation connects well the psalm about praising God in the assembly of the upright with Jesus' warning that merely saying "Lord, Lord" does not guarantee entry into the Kingdom, but that doing the Father's will is necessary. The warning is in accordance with biblical texts, with the note that it does not mean prayer, song, or charismatic gifts are in themselves worthless.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Psalm 111 connects wholehearted praise with the company of the upright, God's covenant, and the practice of his precepts, so praise is not reduced to feeling or outward gesture. Jesus' warning directs the believer toward integrity: prayer and charisms should be joined with obedience to God and a life corresponding to his will.
concerns_en: Opposing the doing of God's will to raising hands, singing, and prayer can be mistakenly understood as disparaging those forms of worship; the issue is separating them from a converted life, not the prayer gesture itself.
The conclusion that evildoers "did not expose evil" is not directly stated in the cited passage from Matthew's Gospel, which emphasizes doing the Father's will.

sections.subtitle_en: Praising God in the assembly of the righteous, not just by raising hands
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar warns that the community of the righteous is not made up of those who only raise their hands and sing, but of those who do the will of God
sections.content_en:
The reading of the psalm follows: “I will praise the Lord with my whole heart in the assembly of the righteous, in their congregation. Great are the works of the Lord…” The psalm continues to magnify the Lord who is gracious and full of compassion, who gives food to those who revere him and remembers his covenant forever.

Grebenar lingers on the **first verse** and asks how one should praise the Lord. He finds the answer in the text itself: with the whole heart, and that in the **assembly of the righteous**, that is, among those who do the will of God. He believes one should meditate on that verse longer, and asks who has experienced shouting, singing, and praising God with their whole heart precisely in a community of people who do God's will.

Then, as he says himself, he becomes “very concrete.” The assembly of the righteous is not a community of people who merely raise their hands in the air and sing to God. There are those who raise their hands, sing, pray, and even pray in tongues, but do not do the will of God.

As confirmation he cites the words of Jesus: “Not everyone who says to me: Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of God, but those who do the will of my Father who is in heaven.” He also recalls the continuation, in which many say on that day that they prophesied and cast out evil spirits in Jesus's name, and he responds to them: “Depart from me, evildoers.”

He concludes that many praised God, but did not live according to his will. They did not expose evil and were evildoers. That is precisely why the psalm speaks explicitly of the assembly of the righteous.

sections.subtitle: Pravednik svaki dan pita: „Što ja trebam danas činiti?“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj slikovito uspoređuje odnos prema Bogu s odnosom djeteta i oca
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim objašnjava tko je pravednik. Sveto pismo, kaže, pravednikom naziva osobu koja ide pravim putem. Jedini pravi put je Isus, a Isus je vršio volju Očevu „skroz do smrti na križu“, a ne svoju.

To, prema voditelju, razumiju samo oni koji **svaki dan pitaju Boga što trebaju činiti** i potom tako i čine. Tko sam sebe vodi i čini po svojoj volji, ne razumije što je volja Božja. „To je jasno kao dan“, ističe.

Svoju misao objašnjava **usporedbom iz obiteljskog života**. Zamislimo dijete koje oca ne pita: „Tata, što ja danas trebam učiniti?“, nego radi što samo hoće. Na kraju dana ipak tvrdi da je izvršilo očevu volju. „Pa jesi li? Možeš tek ako me pitaš. Al' ako me ne pitaš, kako ćeš je izvršiti?“, pita Grebenar.

Isto vrijedi za odnos prema Bogu. Ako ga pitamo za njegovu volju, trudimo se čuti, primiti riječ i vršiti je, tada uistinu vršimo volju Očevu. Ako ne pitamo i ne želimo osluškivati, vršimo svoju volju. Tada smo, kako kaže, „nepokorna djeca, vjerojatno bezakonici, kako ih Isus naziva“.

Zato poziva vjernike da se zauzmu za svoje spasenje. Uz sakramentalni život, postove i slavljenje Gospodina, trebaju Bogu postaviti pitanje: „Što je to tvoja sveta volja, Oče?“ Tko tako čini, ide pravim putem i Sveto pismo ga naziva pravednikom.

**Milost jedinstva**

Na kraju se vraća na psalam i pita tko je iskusio kakva je milost i kakvo jedinstvo biti u zajednici pravednika. To je, ističe, „nešto posebno“. Kada Isus moli za jedinstvo Crkve i apostola, moli za posebnu milost koja dolazi s neba. Nju se, prema Grebenaru, može iskusiti samo u zajednici pravednika koju Bog podiže.

magisterium.assessment: Središnja misao da je Isus savršeno vršio Očevu volju te da su kršćani pozvani živjeti pred Ocem i nasljedovati Krista dobro je usklađena s katoličkim naukom. Ipak, tvrdnje da se Božja volja može vršiti samo ako se Boga izričito pita svakoga dana i da je svatko tko to ne čini stoga neposlušan ili bezakonik pretjerano su kategorične, a jedinstvo Crkve ne treba ograničiti na posebnu zajednicu „pravednika“.
concerns: U odlomku se duhovno korisna praksa svakodnevne molitve i razlučivanja prikazuje kao nužan i jedini način spoznavanja Božje volje. Katekizam potvrđuje da je Krist savršeno vršio Očevu volju i poziva učenike da žive pred Ocem, ali ne podupire zaključak da je izričito svakodnevno pitanje Bogu uvjet za svako vjerno izvršavanje njegove volje.

Izjednačavanje nepostavljanja takva pitanja s neposlušnošću ili bezakonjem može neopravdano opteretiti savjest: odlomak ne razlikuje svjesno odbacivanje Boga od situacije u kojoj osoba nastoji činiti dobro, ali ne razabire jasno što bi trebala učiniti.

Povezivanje posebne milosti jedinstva isključivo sa zajednicom pravednika može zvučati isključivo. Crkveno učenje govori o jedinstvu kao plodu Božjeg djelovanja u Kristu, koje se proteže na učenike i pozvano je okupljati ljude, a ne kao milosti dostupnoj samo skupini koja sebe prepoznaje kao pravednu.
magisterium.enrichment: Kristovo predanje Očevoj volji uzor je kršćanskom životu, ali ne znači da je njegova ljudska volja bila zla ili da je poslušnost puko odricanje od svake osobne prosudbe; Katekizam naglašava da se Očeva volja u Kristu savršeno ispunila upravo kroz njegovu ljudsku volju. Molitva „što je tvoja volja?“ može pomoći vjerniku da je razluči i prihvati, dok se Božja volja također upoznaje kroz Evanđelje, zapovijedi i konkretne dužnosti. Kristova molitva za jedinstvo pokazuje da je jedinstvo dar povezan s Božjim životom i poslanjem Crkve, a ne samo osjećaj pripadnosti određenoj zajednici.

citations.document_title: Synodality in the life and mission of the Church

magisterium.assessment_en: The central thought that Jesus perfectly did the Father's will and that Christians are called to live before the Father and imitate Christ is well aligned with Catholic teaching. However, claims that God's will can only be done if one explicitly asks God every day and that anyone who does not do so is therefore disobedient or an evildoer are excessively categorical, and the unity of the Church should not be restricted to a particular community of the "righteous."
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christ's surrender to the Father's will is the model for Christian life, but it does not mean that his human will was evil or that obedience is mere renunciation of all personal judgment; the Catechism emphasizes that the Father's will was perfectly fulfilled in Christ precisely through his human will. The prayer "what is your will?" can help the believer discern and accept it, while God's will is also known through the Gospel, commandments, and concrete duties. Christ's prayer for unity shows that unity is a gift connected with God's life and the mission of the Church, not merely a feeling of belonging to a particular community.
concerns_en: In the passage, the spiritually useful practice of daily prayer and discernment is presented as the necessary and only way of knowing God's will. The Catechism confirms that Christ perfectly did the Father's will and calls disciples to live before the Father, but does not support the conclusion that explicitly asking God daily is a condition for every faithful execution of his will.

Equating not asking such a question with disobedience or lawlessness can place an unjustified burden on conscience: the passage does not distinguish conscious rejection of God from a situation in which a person strives to do good but does not clearly discern what they should do.

Linking the special grace of unity exclusively to the community of the righteous can sound exclusive. Ecclesial teaching speaks of unity as the fruit of God's action in Christ, extending to the disciples and called to gather people, not as a grace available only to a group that recognizes itself as righteous.

sections.subtitle_en: The righteous person asks every day: “What should I do today?”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host graphically compares the relationship with God to the relationship of a child and a father
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then explains who a righteous person is. Sacred Scripture, he says, calls a righteous person one who walks the right path. The only right path is Jesus, and Jesus did the Father's will “all the way to death on the cross,” not his own.

This, according to the host, is understood only by those who **ask God every day what they should do** and then do so. Whoever leads themselves and acts according to their own will does not understand what the will of God is. “That is as clear as day,” he emphasizes.

He illustrates his thought with a **comparison from family life**. Let us imagine a child who does not ask the father: “Dad, what should I do today?”, but does whatever he wants. At the end of the day, he nonetheless claims that he did the father's will. “Well, did you? You can only do so if you ask me. But if you don't ask me, how will you fulfill it?”, asks Grebenar.

The same applies to the relationship with God. If we ask him for his will, strive to hear, receive the word and fulfill it, then we truly do the will of the Father. If we do not ask and do not want to listen, we do our own will. Then we are, as he says, “disobedient children, probably evildoers, as Jesus calls them.”

Therefore, he calls on the faithful to take responsibility for their salvation. Alongside the sacramental life, fasts, and praising the Lord, they should ask God the question: “What is your holy will, Father?” Whoever does so walks the right path, and Sacred Scripture calls him righteous.

**The grace of unity**

At the end he returns to the psalm and asks who has experienced what kind of grace and what kind of unity it is to be in the community of the righteous. That is, he stresses, “something special.” When Jesus prays for the unity of the Church and the apostles, he prays for a special grace that comes from heaven. It can, according to Grebenar, be experienced only in the community of the righteous that God raises up.

sections.subtitle: Isus na objedu kod farizeja: svjesno je ušao u klopku zbog njihova obraćenja
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar tumači farizejsku podmuklost i Isusovu odluku da ipak dođe na objed
sections.content:
Dnevno evanđelje opisuje subotu u kojoj Isus dolazi na objed u kuću jednog farizejskog prvaka, a prisutni ga vrebaju. Pred njim se pojavljuje čovjek s vodenom bolešću. Isus pita zakonoznance i farizeje: „Je li dopušteno subotom liječiti ili nije?“ Oni šute. Isus bolesnika dotakne, izliječi i otpusti, a zatim im kaže: „Ako komu od vas sin ili vol padne u bunar, neće li ga brže-bolje izvući u dan subotnji?“ Na to mu ne mogu odgovoriti.

Grebenar najprije ističe **podmuklost farizejskog duha**. Pozvali su Isusa na objed upravo zato da ga uhvate. „Pa koja je to podmuklost strašna“, komentira.

Isus je znao da mu pripremaju klopku, a ipak je otišao. Voditelj objašnjava razlog: Isusu je bilo jako stalo da se farizeji obrate. Oni su bili svećenici, ali, kako kaže, „racionalisti“.

Prema Grebenarovu tumačenju, Isus je u molitvi zasigurno osluškivao treba li ići. Bog Otac mu je dopustio da ode jer je unaprijed odredio da tamo dođe čovjek s vodenom bolešću i da se po njemu Bog proslavi. Bog Otac je, kaže voditelj, poslao i toga bolesnika.

Grebenar naglašava da Isus ne bježi. „Ide izravno u konfrontaciju, na prvu liniju.“ Iako ga vrebaju kako bi ga uhvatili na krivoj riječi, Isus ih razoružava jer prvi postavlja pitanje o liječenju subotom.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje da Isus liječenjem subotom čini dobro i izaziva prisutne da preispitaju svoje srce u skladu je s evanđeoskim prikazom i kršćanskim shvaćanjem milosrđa. No tvrdnje da je Otac unaprijed odredio i poslao upravo bolesnika radi tog događaja te da su farizeji kao skupina bili svećenici ne proizlaze iz opisa evanđeoskog prizora koji je ovdje prenesen.
concerns: Evanđeoski sažetak kaže da su prisutni vrebali Isusa, ali ne utvrđuje da je objed organiziran baš kao klopka; to se može ponuditi kao tumačenje okolnosti, ali ne kao izričita činjenica.

Tvrdnja da je Bog Otac poslao bolesnika i unaprijed odredio taj konkretan susret iznesena je kao sigurnost, premda preneseni tekst Evanđelja to ne kaže. Opreznije je reći da Isus u događaju čini djelo milosrđa i objavljuje Božju dobrotu, bez pripisivanja posebnog plana koji tekst ne navodi.

Nazivanje farizeja svećenicima kao skupine nije opravdano u prenesenom evanđeoskom opisu, koji ih razlikuje od zakonoznanaca, ali ih ne naziva svećenicima. Izraz „racionalisti“ također je pojednostavljujuća oznaka ako se njime zanemari da odlomak kritizira konkretno ponašanje prisutnih, a ne nužno svakog farizeja.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusovo liječenje pokazuje da se subotnji počinak ne smije tumačiti tako da sprječava činjenje dobra i milosrđe; kršćanska tradicija u njegovu postupanju vidi obranu čovjeka i izvorno dobro značenje Božjeg zakona. Ivan Zlatousti ističe da Isus ne nastupa samo kao pobjednik u raspravi, nego nastoji potaknuti protivnike na samilost i napustiti tvrdoću srca. Zato se može reći da Isus svjesno ulazi u napetu situaciju radi istine i dobra, ali treba razlikovati takav teološki zaključak od pojedinosti koje evanđeoski tekst izričito ne potvrđuje.
