magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation that Jesus, by healing on the Sabbath, does good and challenges those present to examine their hearts is in accordance with the Gospel portrayal and the Christian understanding of mercy. But claims that the Father predetermined and sent the sick person specifically for that event and that the Pharisees as a group were priests do not arise from the description of the Gospel scene conveyed here.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' healing shows that Sabbath rest must not be interpreted so as to prevent doing good and mercy; Christian tradition sees in his conduct a defense of human beings and the original good meaning of God's law. John Chrysostom emphasizes that Jesus does not act merely as a victor in debate, but seeks to move opponents to compassion and to abandon hardness of heart. Therefore, it can be said that Jesus knowingly enters a tense situation for the sake of truth and good, but one should distinguish such a theological conclusion from details that the Gospel text does not explicitly confirm.
concerns_en: The Gospel summary says those present were watching Jesus closely, but does not establish that the meal was organized specifically as a trap; this can be offered as an interpretation of the circumstances, but not as an explicit fact.

The claim that God the Father sent the sick person and predetermined that specific encounter is asserted as a certainty, although the conveyed text of the Gospel does not say so. It is more cautious to say that Jesus in the event performs an act of mercy and reveals God's goodness, without attributing a specific plan that the text does not state.

Calling the Pharisees priests as a group is not justified in the conveyed Gospel description, which distinguishes them from lawyers, but does not call them priests. The term "rationalists" is also a simplifying label if it overlooks that the passage criticizes the concrete behavior of those present, rather than necessarily every Pharisee.

sections.subtitle_en: Jesus at dinner with the Pharisees: he consciously entered the trap for their conversion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar interprets Pharisaic deceitfulness and Jesus's decision to come to dinner nonetheless
sections.content_en:
The daily gospel describes a sabbath on which Jesus comes to a meal at the house of a leading Pharisee, and those present are watching him closely. In front of him appears a man with dropsy. Jesus asks the lawyers and Pharisees: “Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath, or not?” They remain silent. Jesus touches the sick man, heals him, and lets him go, and then says to them: “If a son or ox of one of you falls into a well, will he not immediately pull him out on the sabbath day?” To this they cannot answer him.

Grebenar first highlights the **deceitfulness of the Pharisaic spirit**. They invited Jesus to the meal precisely to catch him. “What a terrible deceitfulness that is,” he comments.

Jesus knew they were preparing a trap for him, and yet he went. The host explains the reason: Jesus cared deeply that the Pharisees convert. They were priests, but, as he says, “rationalists.”

According to Grebenar's interpretation, Jesus surely listened in prayer whether he should go. God the Father permitted him to go because he had predetermined that the man with dropsy would come there and that God would be glorified through him. God the Father, the host says, sent that sick man as well.

Grebenar stresses that Jesus does not flee. “He goes directly into confrontation, to the front line.” Although they watch him closely to catch him in a wrong word, Jesus disarms them because he is the first to ask the question about healing on the sabbath.

sections.subtitle: Kad je Božje djelo očito, nema više izgovora – i grijeh protiv Duha Svetoga
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj upozorava na komentiranje tuđeg rada i izrugivanje karizmama Duha Svetoga
sections.content:
Farizeji šute, a Isus pred njihovim očima liječi bolesnika. Grebenar objašnjava zašto je taj trenutak važan: radi se o **Božjem djelu**. „I sad je gotovo. Ovi više ne mogu reći da nisu znali.“

Primjenjuje to i na današnje vrijeme. Kada netko posvjedoči da je ozdravio, da se obratio ili da raste u vjeri, nitko više ne može reći da nije znao. Tko nakon toga i dalje napada Isusa, vreba ga i priprema mu zamku i smrt, ide, prema voditelju, „izravno u pakao“.

Ovdje podsjeća na Isusove riječi da će se svi grijesi oprostiti, osim **grijeha protiv Duha Svetoga**. Kao primjer navodi kako bi farizeji, nakon što je Isus ozdravio čovjeka, govorili: „Ovo nije od Boga, Bog ne liječi subotom.“ Isusu su doista prigovarali i da ljude oslobađa Belzebulom. Nazivati Božje djelo, kojim se čovjek oslobađa od zloga i ozdravlja, đavlovim djelom upravo je grijeh protiv Duha Svetoga.

Zato upozorava vjernike da dobro paze što rade i govore jer mnogi sebi daju previše slobode. Iznosi i vlastito načelo, koje je, kaže, mnogo puta ponovio: ne dolazi u obzir da bi komentirao tuđi rad. Ako netko moli, ako ljudi ozdravljaju i događaju se znamenja i čudesa, njegov savjet je: „Šuti i ne javljaj se.“

Oštro govori i o onima koji se, među ostalim na društvenim mrežama, izruguju drugima nazivajući ih „karizmaticima“. „Ha, to ćeš Bogu reći“, poručuje. Kao primjer navodi apostola Pavla, koji je bio pun karizmi Duha Svetoga i pokrstio „pola Europe“. Bog, zaključuje, nije dao karizme zato da bi im se izrugivao netko racionalan, farizejske vjere.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak is djelomično usklađen: ispravno prepoznaje ozbiljnost pripisivanja Božjeg oslobađajućeg djelovanja zlu, ali preširoko poistovjećuje kritiku ili sumnju s grijehom protiv Duha Svetoga i neprimjereno zaključuje da takvi ljudi idu „izravno u pakao“. Katolički nauk grijeh protiv Duha Svetoga povezuje s tvrdokornim odbijanjem Božjeg oproštenja i spasenja, a ne daje govorniku pravo da pojedincima unaprijed presudi vječnu sudbinu.
concerns: Isusovo upozorenje u evanđeljima odnosi se na pripisivanje Božjem Duhu djela koja se svjesno i zlonamjerno proglašavaju djelom zloga; ne znači da je svako neslaganje, oprez ili kritičko ispitivanje navodnog čuda grijeh protiv Duha Svetoga.

Tvrdnja da osoba koja nastavi napadati Isusa nakon svjedočanstva ide „izravno u pakao“ pretjerano je sigurna presuda o konkretnim osobama; nauk naglašava da je neoprostivost povezana s odbijanjem pokajanja i Božjeg milosrđa.
Savjet „šuti i ne javljaj se“ može odvratiti od razboritog razlučivanja: čudesna ozdravljenja i karizmatske tvrdnje ne treba unaprijed ni odbacivati ni prihvaćati bez provjere.

Povezivanje podsmijeha karizmatskim pojavama s farizejskim duhom može nepravedno izjednačiti ruganje s legitimnim pitanjima ili oprezom; tvrdnja da je Pavao „pokrstio pola Europe“ također je neprecizna i nije potkrijepljena raspoloživim izvorima.
magisterium.enrichment: Ivan Pavao II. objašnjava da se bit grijeha protiv Duha Svetoga ne iscrpljuje u izgovaranju uvredljivih riječi, nego se tiče odbijanja spasenja koje Bog nudi po Duhu; Katekizam dodaje da Bog ne postavlja granice svojem milosrđu, ali čovjek može odbijati oproštenje ako se ne želi pokajati. Zato je primjereno ozbiljno upozoriti na zlonamjerno izvrtanje očitoga dobra, ali treba razlikovati takvu tvrdokornost od iskrenog razlučivanja i ne presuđivati tuđe vječno spasenje.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is partially aligned: it correctly recognizes the gravity of attributing God's liberating action to evil, but too broadly equates criticism or doubt with the sin against the Holy Spirit and inappropriately concludes that such people go "directly to hell." Catholic doctrine connects the sin against the Holy Spirit with the obstinate refusal of God's forgiveness and salvation, and does not give the speaker the right to judge individuals' eternal destiny in advance.
magisterium.enrichment_en: John Paul II explains that the essence of the sin against the Holy Spirit is not exhausted in uttering offensive words, but concerns the refusal of the salvation God offers through the Spirit; the Catechism adds that God sets no limits to his mercy, but man can reject forgiveness if he refuses to repent. Therefore, it is appropriate to give a serious warning against the malicious distortion of evident good, but one must distinguish such obstinacy from sincere discernment and not judge the eternal salvation of others.
concerns_en: Jesus' warning in the Gospels refers to attributing to God's Spirit works that are knowingly and maliciously declared to be the work of the evil one; it does not mean that every disagreement, caution, or critical examination of an alleged miracle is a sin against the Holy Spirit.

The claim that a person who continues to attack Jesus after a testimony goes "directly to hell" is an overly confident judgment about specific individuals; doctrine emphasizes that unpardonability is connected with the refusal of repentance and God's mercy.
The advice "be quiet and don't speak up" can discourage prudent discernment: miraculous healings and charismatic claims should neither be rejected in advance nor accepted without verification.

Linking mockery of charismatic phenomena with the pharisaic spirit can unfairly equate ridicule with legitimate questions or caution; the claim that Paul "baptized half of Europe" is also imprecise and unsupported by available sources.

sections.subtitle_en: When God's work is obvious, there are no more excuses – and the sin against the Holy Spirit
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host warns against commenting on others' work and mocking the charisms of the Holy Spirit
sections.content_en:
The Pharisees remain silent, and Jesus heals the sick man before their eyes. Grebenar explains why that moment is important: it is a **work of God**. “And now it is finished. These can no longer say they did not know.”

He applies this to the present day as well. When someone testifies that they were healed, that they converted, or that they are growing in faith, no one can say any longer that they did not know. Whoever after that continues to attack Jesus, lurks for him, and sets a trap and death for him goes, according to the host, “directly to hell.”

Here he recalls the words of Jesus that all sins will be forgiven except the **sin against the Holy Spirit**. As an example, he mentions how the Pharisees, after Jesus healed the man, would say: “This is not from God, God does not heal on the sabbath.” Indeed, they also reproached Jesus for casting out demons by Beelzebul. Calling God's work, by which a person is delivered from evil and healed, the devil's work is precisely the sin against the Holy Spirit.

Therefore, he warns the faithful to pay close attention to what they do and say, because many take too much liberty. He also states his own principle, which he says he has repeated many times: it is out of the question for him to comment on someone else's work. If someone prays, if people are healed, and signs and wonders happen, his advice is: “Be quiet and do not speak up.”

He also speaks sharply about those who, among other places on social networks, mock others by calling them “charismatics.” “Ha, you will say that to God,” he tells them. As an example he cites the apostle Paul, who was full of charisms of the Holy Spirit and baptized “half of Europe.” God, he concludes, did not give charisms so that someone rational, of Pharisaic faith, could mock them.

sections.subtitle: Kvasac farizejski danas: oprez i ustrajnost do kraja
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar upozorava na kvasac farizejski i poziva na čvrstu vjeru
sections.content:
Grebenar ističe da farizeji u Svetom pismu nisu mogli čitati o nekim farizejima prije sebe. Oni su **prvi dali taj negativan primjer**. Danas, međutim, u Svetom pismu čitamo o farizejima, a mnogi i dalje imaju upravo takvu, farizejsku vjeru.

Zato ponavlja Isusovo upozorenje: „Čuvaj se kvasca farizejskog.“ Prema njegovim riječima, kod osobe takva duha potreban je veliki oprez i ne treba joj se otvarati jer se može izgubiti vjera. Njezina priča „ukvasa“ čovjeka i okrene ga na drugu stranu. Voditelj to slikovito opisuje: vidiš čudo, vidiš živog Isusa, vidiš da se nešto događa, a farizej te, ako ga poslušaš, okrene na drugu stranu.

Na kraju tumačenja poziva vjernike da svjedoče, ali i da budu čvrsti u vjeri. Pritom se nadovezuje na tumačenje iz prethodnog dana: treba uzeti **štit vjere**, imati veliko povjerenje u Gospodina i ne posustati nimalo. „Oni koji ustraju do kraja, ti će se spasiti. Tako piše u Svetom pismu“, zaključuje i završava tumačenje za taj dan.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je djelomično do uglavnom usklađen: biblijsko upozorenje na „kvasac farizejski“ i poziv na ustrajnost u vjeri imaju čvrst kršćanski temelj, ali prikaz farizeja kao skupine kojoj se općenito ne treba otvarati može poticati nepovjerenje i pojednostavljivanje. Ustrajnost do kraja jest važna za spasenje, no nije samodostatno ljudsko postignuće nego vjernost koja se živi uz Božju pomoć.
concerns: Tvrdnja da su farizeji bili „prvi“ koji su dali takav negativan primjer nije jasno utemeljena u raspoloživim izvorima i preširoka je kao povijesna tvrdnja.

Upozorenje na lažno učenje ne bi trebalo pretvoriti u opću zabranu povjerenja ili razgovora s ljudima označenima kao „farizeji“; treba razlučivati konkretno učenje i postupke, a ne unaprijed otpisivati osobe.
„Oni koji ustraju do kraja, ti će se spasiti“ vjerno prenosi biblijski motiv, ali bez konteksta može zvučati kao da se spasenje zaslužuje samo osobnom čvrstoćom.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusovo upozorenje na farizejski kvasac poziva na budnost prema licemjerju i učenju koje udaljava od Boga; ono nije dozvola za prezir prema osobama niti zamjena za razborito prosuđivanje. Crkveno tumačenje povezuje ustrajnost s vjernošću Kristu u kušnjama, a ne s pouzdanjem u vlastitu snagu: Ivan Pavao II. poziva vjernike da ostanu čvrsti u evanđeoskoj istini i da mole za dar Duha snage.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is partially to mainly aligned: the biblical warning against the "leaven of the Pharisees" and the call to perseverance in faith have a solid Christian foundation, but portraying the Pharisees as a group to whom one should generally not open up can encourage distrust and oversimplification. Perseverance to the end is indeed important for salvation, but it is not a self-sufficient human achievement rather a fidelity lived with God's help.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' warning against the leaven of the Pharisees calls for vigilance against hypocrisy and teaching that leads away from God; it is not a license for contempt toward persons, nor a substitute for prudent judgment. Ecclesial interpretation connects perseverance with fidelity to Christ in trials, rather than with reliance on one's own strength: John Paul II calls the faithful to remain firm in evangelical truth and to pray for the gift of the Spirit of fortitude.
concerns_en: The claim that the Pharisees were the "first" to set such a negative example is not clearly grounded in available sources and is too broad as a historical claim.

Warning against false teaching should not be turned into a general prohibition of trust or conversation with people labeled as "Pharisees"; one should discern specific teaching and actions, rather than writing people off in advance.
"Those who persevere to the end, they will be saved" faithfully conveys the biblical motif, but without context can sound as if salvation is earned by personal steadfastness alone.

sections.subtitle_en: The Pharisaic leaven today: caution and perseverance to the end
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar warns against the Pharisaic leaven and calls for steadfast faith
sections.content_en:
Grebenar points out that the Pharisees in Sacred Scripture could not read about any Pharisees before them. They were **the first to set that negative example**. Today, however, we read in Sacred Scripture about the Pharisees, yet many continue to have precisely that kind of Pharisaic faith.

Therefore, he repeats Jesus's warning: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.” According to his words, with a person of such a spirit great caution is required and one should not open up to them, because one can lose faith. Their talk “leavens” a person and turns them in another direction. The host describes this vividly: you see a miracle, you see the living Jesus, you see that something is happening, and the Pharisee, if you listen to him, turns you in another direction.

At the end of the exposition, he invites the faithful to witness, but also to be firm in faith. In doing so, he builds on the exposition from the previous day: one must take the **shield of faith**, have great confidence in the Lord, and not waver in the least. “Those who persevere to the end will be saved. That is what Sacred Scripture says,” he concludes and ends the exposition for that day.

sections.subtitle: Promocije knjige „Isus Lider“ i predstavljanje domoljubne inicijative od Ljubuškog do Imotskog
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje termine i lokacije promocija knjige Isus Lider
sections.content:
Nakon tumačenja Grebenar donosi praktične obavijesti. Toga dana, **30. listopada**, nalazi se u **Ljubuškom, u hotelu Bigeste**. Program počinje u 19 sati molitvom krunice. Slijede promocija knjige **„Isus Lider“, treći dio** i predstavljanje domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora. Moli vjernike iz Hercegovine da obavijest podijele na društvenim mrežama, „pa neka dođe koga milost pozove“.

Najavljuje i ostale termine:

- **31. listopada:** Prozor-Rama, dvorana hidroelektrane Rama
- **ponedjeljak, 2. studenoga:** Biograd na Moru, hotel Ilirija
- **utorak, 3. studenoga:** Solin, hotel President
- **srijeda, 4. studenoga:** Imotski, Pučko otvoreno učilište Imotski

Poziva sve da postanu članovi **domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora**. Prijava se obavlja ispunjavanjem obrasca na web stranici, a za sva otvorena pitanja dostupni su brojevi mobitela za Hrvatsku te za Bosnu i Hercegovinu.

Zahvaljuje svima koji doniraju i podržavaju rad medija. Poziva gledatelje da, kad se sjete, uplate „poneku donaciju Bogu na slavu“, uz napomenu: „Mi znamo što ćemo s tim sredstvima.“

magisterium.assessment: Najave predstavljanja knjige, domoljubne inicijative i prikupljanja donacija same po sebi ne proturječe katoličkom nauku, a iz sažetka se ne vidi dovoljno sadržaja inicijative da bi se mogla teološki prosuditi. Izraz „donacija Bogu na slavu” može biti pobožna namjera, ali ne zamjenjuje jasnoću o tome kome se sredstva daju i kako se koriste.
concerns: Napomena „Mi znamo što ćemo s tim sredstvima” može slušateljima ostaviti nejasnoću o namjeni donacija; to je pitanje odgovornog upravljanja i transparentnosti, a ne samo po sebi dokaz doktrinarnog odstupanja.
Budući da nije opisan sadržaj inicijative Ora et Labora, ne može se procijeniti jesu li njezini ciljevi i metode u skladu s katoličkim naukom.
magisterium.enrichment: Donacija može biti čin kršćanske velikodušnosti ako se daje slobodno i služi dobrom djelu, ali pobožno pozivanje na Božju slavu ne oslobađa organizatore obveze da objasne način upravljanja darovima. Ni domoljubna svrha nije sama po sebi jamstvo kršćanske usklađenosti: njezine konkretne poruke i postupci trebaju poštovati dostojanstvo svake osobe i opće dobro. Sažetak ne pruža pojedinosti potrebne za daljnji sud.
magisterium.assessment_en: Announcements of a book presentation, a patriotic initiative, and the collection of donations do not in themselves contradict Catholic teaching, and the summary does not disclose enough content of the initiative to judge it theologically. The expression "donation to the glory of God" can be a pious intention, but does not replace clarity regarding to whom funds are given and how they are used.
magisterium.enrichment_en: A donation can be an act of Christian generosity if given freely and serving a good work, but a pious reference to God's glory does not exempt organizers from the obligation to explain how gifts are administered. Nor is a patriotic purpose in itself a guarantee of Christian alignment: its specific messages and actions should respect the dignity of every person and the common good. The summary does not provide details needed for further judgment.
concerns_en: The remark "We know what we will do with those funds" can leave listeners in uncertainty regarding the purpose of the donations; this is a question of responsible stewardship and transparency, and not in itself proof of doctrinal departure.
Because the content of the Ora et Labora initiative is not described, it cannot be evaluated whether its goals and methods align with Catholic teaching.

sections.subtitle_en: Book promotions for “Jesus Leader” and presentation of the patriotic initiative from Ljubuški to Imotski
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the dates and locations of the book promotions for Jesus Leader
sections.content_en:
Following the exposition, Grebenar delivers practical notices. On that day, **October 30**, he is in **Ljubuški, at the Hotel Bigeste**. The program begins at 7:00 PM with the recitation of the Rosary. There follow the book promotion for **“Jesus Leader”, part three** and the presentation of the patriotic initiative Ora et Labora. He asks the faithful from Hercegovina to share the announcement on social networks, “so let whoever grace calls come.”

He also announces the other dates:

- **October 31:** Prozor-Rama, hall of the Rama hydroelectric power plant
- **Monday, November 2:** Biograd na Moru, Hotel Ilirija
- **Tuesday, November 3:** Solin, Hotel President
- **Wednesday, November 4:** Imotski, Pučko otvoreno učilište Imotski

He invites everyone to become members of the **patriotic initiative Ora et Labora**. Registration is carried out by filling out the form on the website, and for all open questions mobile phone numbers are available for Croatia and for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

He thanks everyone who donates and supports the work of the media. He invites viewers, when it comes to mind, to make “a donation for the glory of God,” with the remark: “We know what we will do with those funds.”

sections.subtitle: Poziv na javnu molitvu krunice 7. studenoga i završni blagoslov
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zaziva završni blagoslov u ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga
sections.content:
Grebenar napominje da toga dana nije pripremio uobičajeno svjedočanstvo jer je na putu. Obećava da će to učiniti sljedeći dan.

Upućuje zatim **poziv na javnu molitvu krunice**. Inicijativa dolazi na zamolbu Hrvata izvan domovine, odnosno njihove udruge u Njemačkoj. Molitva je predviđena za **7. studenoga, prvu subotu u mjesecu**. Poziv je upućen vjernicima u dijaspori, u domovini i u Bosni i Hercegovini: „Pokreni molitvu krunice na trgu tamo gdje živiš.“

Emisija završava blagoslovom. Voditelj zaziva da se sveta Majka sa svojim Sinom i svetim Josipom udostoji blagosloviti sve gledatelje i slušatelje, u ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga.

Na kraju podsjeća da se mogu nabaviti prvi, drugi i treći dio knjige **„Isus Lider“**. Kupnjom se pomaže dovršetak **međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira**. Gledatelje poziva da svaki dan prate Ora et Laboru, uz poruku: „Neka je sve na veću slavu Božju.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na zajedničku javnu molitvu krunice u skladu je s katoličkom pobožnošću, a iskazivanje molitve za Marijin zagovor i zazivanje Božjeg blagoslova mogu biti prikladni izrazi vjere. Izraz da Majka Božja, njezin Sin i sveti Josip blagoslove slušatelje bilo bi teološki jasnije razumjeti kao molbu za Božji blagoslov i zagovor svetaca, a ne kao pripisivanje neovisne božanske moći Mariji ili Josipu.
concerns: Završna formulacija o blagoslovu može biti dvoznačna ako se shvati kao da Marija i sveti Josip blagoslivljaju vlastitom, od Boga neovisnom moći; sažetak ne pokazuje da je to bila namjera govornika.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno učiteljstvo posebno cijeni zajedničku molitvu krunice, koja povezuje molitelje i vodi ih razmatranju Kristova života, smrti i uskrsnuća. Mariju se zaziva da zagovara vjernike kod svoga Sina; njezin zagovor ne zamjenjuje Kristovo jedinstveno posredništvo.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to communal public prayer of the Rosary is in accordance with Catholic devotion, and expressing prayer for Mary's intercession and invoking God's blessing can be appropriate expressions of faith. The expression that the Mother of God, her Son, and Saint Joseph bless listeners would be theologically clearer if understood as a request for God's blessing and the intercession of the saints, rather than attributing independent divine power to Mary or Joseph.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's Magisterium particularly values communal prayer of the Rosary, which unites those praying and leads them to meditate on Christ's life, death, and resurrection. Mary is invoked to intercede for the faithful with her Son; her intercession does not replace Christ's unique mediation.
concerns_en: The concluding formulation about blessing can be ambiguous if understood as Mary and Saint Joseph blessing by their own power independent of God; the summary does not show that this was the speaker's intention.

sections.subtitle_en: Call for public recitation of the Rosary on November 7 and final blessing
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invokes the final blessing in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit
sections.content_en:
Grebenar notes that on that day he did not prepare the usual testimony because he is traveling. He promises to do so the next day.

He then issues a **call for the public recitation of the Rosary**. The initiative comes at the request of Croats outside the homeland, that is, their association in Germany. The prayer is planned for **November 7, the first Saturday of the month**. The invitation is addressed to the faithful in the diaspora, in the homeland, and in Bosnia and Herzegovina: “Start the recitation of the Rosary in the square where you live.”

The show concludes with a blessing. The host invokes that the holy Mother with her Son and Saint Joseph deign to bless all viewers and listeners, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

Finally, he reminds that the first, second, and third parts of the book **“Jesus Leader”** can be purchased. The purchase helps the completion of the **Queen of Peace International Educational Center**. He invites viewers to follow Ora et Labora every day, with the message: “May all be for the greater glory of God.”

iterations.theme_en: Exposition of the holy word: The Day of Christ as the day of judgment and mercy, the assembly of the righteous who do the will of God, the Pharisaic spirit and the sin against the Holy Spirit, announcements, and final blessing
